title: Digit DP
tagline: Count numbers in a range with a digit property by building them digit by digit.

intuition.analogy: Filling in a number on a form one box at a time, left to right. As long as your prefix matches the upper bound's prefix, the next digit is capped; the moment you go lower, all remaining boxes are free to be 0–9.
paragraphs: Digit DP counts how many numbers in [0, N] (or a range) satisfy some property of their digits — like 'no two adjacent equal digits' or 'digit sum divisible by k'. Iterating to N would be far too slow for big N.

You build the number digit by digit from the most significant end, carrying a small state: the position, whatever property accumulator you need, and a 'tight' flag indicating whether the prefix is still equal to N's prefix (which bounds the current digit).
A 'started' flag handles leading zeros when they matter. Memoise on (position, state, tight, started) — though tight states are usually visited once and need not be cached.
intuition.keyIdea: Build digits left-to-right; a 'tight' flag caps the next digit until you drop below the bound, then everything is free.

steps.title: Represent N as digits
steps.detail: Store N's digits in an array, most significant first.

steps.title: Recurse position by position
steps.detail: solve(pos, state, tight): try each digit d from 0 to (tight ? N[pos] : 9), updating state and tightness (tight && d == N[pos]).

steps.title: Memoise the free states
steps.detail: When not tight (and not constrained by leading zeros), the result depends only on (pos, state) — cache it.

pitfalls: Don't memoise tight states — they depend on the exact bound and recur only once.
Handle leading zeros with a 'started' flag when zeros shouldn't count as a digit.

problems.title: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
problems.statement: Count numbers with all distinct digits below 10^n.
problems.hint: Digit DP with a used-digit mask (or combinatorics).

approach: Count numbers in [0, 10^n) whose digits are all distinct. This is a counting-principle (the combinatorial heart of digit DP).
For length 1 there are 10. For each additional digit the first digit has 9 choices (no leading zero) and each subsequent has one fewer available digit: 9·9, 9·9·8, …. Sum across lengths.

problems.title: Numbers At Most N Given Digit Set
problems.statement: Count numbers ≤ N using only allowed digits.
problems.hint: Tight-bound digit DP over the allowed set.

approach: Count positive integers <= n built only from the allowed digit set. Split by length.

Numbers with fewer digits than n: m^len for each shorter length (m = set size). For the same length, scan n's digits left to right: at each position count allowed digits strictly smaller (each frees the rest to be anything → ·m^remaining), then continue only if the exact digit is allowed; add 1 at the end if n itself is fully constructible.

problems.title: Count of Integers
problems.statement: Count integers in [low, high] with digit-sum in a range.

approach: Define f(x) = count of integers in [0, x] whose digit sum lies in [min_sum, max_sum]. The answer is f(num2) - f(num1 - 1).
Digit DP over the decimal string with state (position, running sum, tight). Prune when the sum exceeds max_sum; memoise the non-tight states. Take everything modulo 1e9+7.

problems.title: Non-negative Integers without Consecutive Ones
problems.statement: Count numbers ≤ n with no consecutive 1s in binary.
problems.hint: Binary digit DP carrying the previous bit.

approach: Count integers in [0, n] whose binary representation has no two consecutive 1s. Digit DP over the bits (most significant first).
State (position, previous bit, tight). Forbid placing a 1 right after a 1; otherwise try both bits within the tight bound.

problems.title: Classy Numbers
problems.statement: Count numbers in a range with ≤ 3 non-zero digits.
problems.hint: State = count of non-zero digits so far.
problems.tests: Digit DP with a counter state.

approach: A 'classy' number has at most three non-zero digits. Define f(x) = count of classy integers in [1, x]; the answer is f(R) - f(L-1).
Digit DP over x's decimal digits with state (position, count of non-zero digits used, tight). Stop a branch once the count would exceed 3.
